I absolutely do not recommend Amarok Dog Training Center.
At first, everything seemed very professional. But on the first Saturday, when we went to train with him (as they instructed), my husband and I noticed something worrying: Po was very thin (his ribs were showing) and one of his paws looked injured.
We mentioned it to the trainer, and he downplayed everything. Even when I asked if he was eating well, he laughed and assured me that he was "eating VERY well." Even so, we left with a very bad feeling.
During the following week, I repeatedly requested videos of the supposed "socialization" and activities they claim to do. I never received any of that. They only sent two very short videos of Po practicing commands. None of the multiple activities they promised.
The following Saturday, the situation was much worse. Po was even thinner, his paws were more injured, and his teeth showed obvious wear. Again, they assured us that "everything was fine" and that a veterinarian was checking on him, but they never provided any evidence or follow-up.

We requested a veterinary report that same day (Saturday). They never sent it. We had to insist, and even then, we received nothing. At that point, we decided to pick up our dog immediately. Their response was that we first had to cancel the course… which we found completely unreasonable, so we didn't pay for it.

When we finally picked up Po, he was in much worse condition: his mouth was sore with canker sores, his teeth were yellow and worn, he had diarrhea, and he was much thinner.

Seeing that he wasn't improving over the following days, we took him to the vet, and he was diagnosed with:
Giardiasis
Coronavirus
A lesion on his lip (possibly traumatic).

I shared these results with Amarok so they would be aware (since these are contagious diseases), and I never received a response.

They also refused to let me see the facilities where he slept, and I was never able to verify the activities they claimed to be doing. It all remained just well-written messages, but without any real evidence.

Honestly, our perception is that the dogs spend far too much time locked up without proper care.

Yes, he did learn some commands, but it's definitely not worth it considering the condition it was in and the lack of communication.

I absolutely do not recommend this place. My experience was terrible, and what's worse, they put my dog's health at risk.

She entered the camp weighing 23 kg and was returned to me a month later weighing only 16 kg. Losing 7 kg in 30 days is a loss of almost 30% of her body mass; it's an alarming situation where her ribs and spine were completely visible.

The most outrageous thing was the response from the customer service representative. When I asked for an explanation about her diet, she simply said that 'it's normal for dogs to lose 10% of their weight at the camp.' Not only is this a technical lie, but in my dog's case, it was three times what they consider 'normal.'

When I confronted the situation, the response was to become defensive instead of taking responsibility for the obvious lack of care and nutrition. In addition to the physical injuries, my dog ​​returned with strange and fearful behavior, which makes me suspect further abuse.

At first, everything is friendly, but when a serious problem arises, they disappear. It has been a long and difficult process to help her regain her weight and confidence. Don't waste your money, and above all, don't risk your pets' lives at this place. It's a complete lack of ethics and humanity.
